standard_prerequisites: the naive cotangent complex NL of a ring map and Ext groups over D(B)
the two-term complex representing NL of a quotient presentation (Algebra, Section algebra-section-netherlander)

the More on Algebra lemmas: the determinant of the Jacobian matrix acts trivially on the displayed matrix complex (more-algebra-lemma-silly) and a surjection of two-term complexes transfers vanishing of multiplication (more-algebra-lemma-two-term-surjection-map-zero)
distinguished triangles in the derived category and the long exact Ext sequence
core_obligations: Prove that the determinant g of the m-by-m Jacobian matrix annihilates Ext^1_B(NL_{B/A}, N) for every B-module N, and that when n = m multiplication by g on NL_{B/A} is zero in D(B)
proof_roadmap: Let K be the two-term complex given by the Jacobian matrix T; More on Algebra shows multiplication by g on K is zero in D(B).

Compare NL_{B/A} with the truncated complex L = J/J^2 to the Bdx_i summands through the quotient map NL to L and the surjection of complexes K to L; the More on Algebra surjection lemma makes multiplication by g on L zero in D(B).
The distinguished triangle B^{n-m}[0] to NL_{B/A} to L gives a surjection on Ext^1 from L to NL, so g annihilates Ext^1_B(NL_{B/A}, N).
When n = m the quotient map NL to L is an isomorphism, giving part (2).
difficulty_reason: H3: three-term comparison diagram NL to L to K in the derived category, with vanishing transferred across a surjection of complexes and a distinguished triangle controlling Ext^1.
